hints: Notice only the vertical part of the launch velocity lifts the ball to height $H$, so start with the vertical component $v\sin\alpha$.
At maximum height $H$ the vertical component of velocity is momentarily zero while horizontal motion continues, so apply vertical kinematics with acceleration $-g$.
Use $v_y^2 = u_y^2 + 2a_ys$ with $u_y = v\sin\alpha$, $v_y = 0$ and $s = H$, then rearrange for $H$ and check which option has $v^2/g$ form.
walkthrough: Resolve the launch velocity: horizontal component is $v\cos\alpha$ and vertical component is $u_y = v\sin\alpha$. Only $u_y$ determines $H$.
Consider vertical motion up to the top of the dashed trajectory. Take upwards as positive, so displacement $s = H$, acceleration $a = -g$, and final vertical velocity $v_y = 0$.
Rearrange: $2gH = (v\sin\alpha)^2$, so $H = (v\sin\alpha)^2 / 2g$. The $v^2/g$ combination gives units of $\text{m}$, as required for a height.

A.explanation: This has units of time, not length, and misses the square on the vertical speed needed from $v^2 = u^2 + 2as$.

B.explanation: This is inverted with $g$ on top and $v$ below, so it does not give a height in $\text{m}$ and does not match the kinematics of the vertical motion.

C.explanation: Using initial vertical speed $v\sin\alpha$ and $0 = (v\sin\alpha)^2 - 2gH$ gives $H = (v\sin\alpha)^2 / 2g$.

D.explanation: This has $g^2/v$ which gives units of $\text{m s}^{-3}$, so it cannot equal the height $H$ in $\text{m}$.
